title: Beyond Differentiability: Neurosymbolic Learning with Black-Box Programs

review.summary: The paper introduces ISED, a neurosymbolic learning framework that uses black-box programs written in general-purpose languages like Python, avoiding the constraints of differentiable logic programming. Diverse benchmark suite covering synthetic, neurosymbolic, and real-world tasks
Demonstrated superior accuracy (30% improvement) over neural baselines and Scallop in many benchmarks
Clear explanation of the structural mapping interface and sampling-based gradient approximation
weaknesses: Lacks detailed mathematical justification for the sampling-based gradient approximation method
No comparison with other non-differentiable neurosymbolic frameworks (e.g., DeepProbLog, NeurASP)

Limited discussion of computational efficiency compared to differentiable methods
